title: Prove multi-contour vector model before boolean tools ship
outcome: Existing vectors migrate to document v6 without visual change, while a multi-contour vector can render a subtract-created hole and survive save/reopen before production boolean commands are exposed.
before: The current VectorLayer model stores one contour only, so boolean results with holes or disjoint pieces cannot be represented truthfully.
after: The document/rendering model can represent and round-trip multi-contour vectors with explicit fill behavior without regressing existing single-contour files; no user-facing boolean controls ship in this packet.
acceptance: A v5 single-contour vector opens through the v6 migration path and renders pixel-identically to the pre-migration baseline.
A multi-contour test vector containing an outer contour and inner hole renders the hole correctly under the chosen explicit fill rule.
The same multi-contour vector survives serialize/save and reopen without geometry, fill, stroke, or contour loss.
Validation rejects malformed contour arrays, non-finite coordinates, and out-of-contract contour/node counts.
Existing document-model, editor, rendering, export, TypeScript and build gates remain green.
No user-visible boolean command or decorative control is introduced in Phase 0.
evidence: Multi-contour rendering test or pixel evidence showing an actual hole

builder.notes: Not assigned until Governor activates the packet.

critic.notes: Phase 0 exposes no new user-facing UI; rendering evidence is handled by verifier.

delta.before: Single-contour VectorLayer cannot truthfully store boolean results containing holes or disjoint contours.
